A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same DDPN research work, with 33 readable pages and complete Appendices A–D. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v3 reports original simulations, experiments on four real-world datasets, OOD detection results, and additional analyses and GLM results in the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark and OOD experiments and the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The DDPN architecture, objectives in Equations 2–3, stop-gradient operation and ensemble inference are unchanged. The corrected derivative in Section 3.3 fixes the mathematics describing the existing objective rather than introducing a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions use Length of Stay, COCO-People, Inventory and Amazon Reviews, the same synthetic scenarios, and the same Amazon Reviews versus King James Bible OOD evaluation.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Poisson, Negative Binomial, Gaussian, Faithful Gaussian, Natural Gaussian and beta-Gaussian baselines. The Poisson, NB and Double Poisson GLM comparisons in Appendix B.4.2 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same splits, model configurations, training budgets, validation-based checkpoint selection, metrics and variance-threshold OOD procedure. No revised experimental settings are reported.

E4.justification: Both retain the same misspecification tests, beta training-dynamics experiment, moment-approximation analysis, inverse-dispersion initialization study, sharpness analysis and predictive-distribution case studies.

E5.justification: The five-model neural evaluations, ten-repeat OOD holdout resampling and five-model GLM evaluations retain their existing uncertainty reporting. No run counts, seed information or statistical procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Reported numerical and qualitative results match throughout, including Tables 2–5 and appendix figures. For example, Table 2 gives the beta=1 DDPN ensemble COCO-People MAE/CRPS as 0.959/0.712 in both versions; Table 3 retains the beta=0.5 DDPN AUROC of 0.887.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 corrects the beta-NLL derivative with respect to predicted inverse dispersion. v3 omits gamma_hat_i^(-beta) from the residual term; v5 includes this multiplier, making the derivative consistent with Equation 3 and its stop-gradient convention. Other definitions, assumptions, propositions and appendix proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about full heteroscedasticity, learnable loss attenuation, beta-controlled attenuation and superior accuracy, calibration and OOD detection.

C2.justification: Results interpretations and applicability qualifications are unchanged. Appendix A.2 retains the limitations concerning high counts, moment approximations, optimization stability and evidence from only one OOD task.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 preserves the same implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, preprocessing and data-access details. Code and dataset access disclosures are unchanged, including the nonpublic status of Inventory.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to Gaussian regressors, deep ensembles and count GLMs are unchanged. The proceedings-label edit does not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: The first-page proceedings label changes from '41st' to '42nd' International Conference on Machine Learning, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Body prose, terminology and section and appendix organization are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Figures 1–32 and Tables 1–5 retain their designs, captions, axes, structure and placement. The page and column organization is unchanged; the corrected derivative entails only incidental local text reflow.

improvement.justification: v5 resolves a mathematical inconsistency by restoring the missing inverse-dispersion multiplier in Section 3.3, making the stated derivative agree with the existing stop-gradient objective. This improves technical correctness and reduces potential implementation confusion, while the method, evidence, conclusions and limitations remain unchanged.
